items.question: On which day does its trading period begin?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the 252 formation days.

explain.text: Formation takes days 2,016 to 2,267, so trading begins on day 2,268. It ends just before day 2,394.

items.question: How many portfolios trade in month 9?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the portfolios started in the last six months.

byKey.ten: You counted every portfolio since month 0. Those before month 4 have finished.

explain.text: Portfolios 4 to 9 are inside their six months, so 6 trade at once. From month 5 on it is always six.

feedback.generic: Not quite. The mean is 0, so average the squares and take the root.

items.prose: Twenty pairs are nominated; 15 open. The payoffs add to £1.20.
items.question: What is the return on employed capital?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide by the pairs that opened.

byKey.comm: 0.06 divides by all 20: that is committed.

explain.text: Employed divides £1.20 by the 15 opened pairs: 0.08. Committed would be 0.06.

items.prose: Our top 20 earn about 1.00% a month committed, with no wait.
items.question: What is that as a compounded annual return?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Raise 1.01 to the 12th power and subtract 1.

explain.text: 1.01¹² − 1 = 0.1268, about 12.7% a year. The one-day wait brings it down to about 9.4%.

items.prose: The generator keeps a fraction φ of each planted gap every day. Suppose `half_life` were 4 days instead of 8.
items.question: What would φ be, to four places?

byKey.quarter: You divided 0.5 by 4. Take the 4th root instead.
byKey.eight: 0.917 is φ for a half-life of 8.

explain.text: φ⁴ = 0.5 gives φ = 0.8409. A shorter half-life means faster convergence, so more round trips per cycle.
